text: The public submission surface is the Plugins dashboard at platform.openai.com/plugins: upload a plugin ZIP, clear automated metadata/skill/MCP checks, submit for review, then publish after approval.
Before submitting any plugin, the developer must complete individual or business identity verification in Organization Settings; publishing under an unverified identity is rejected.

The signed-in OpenAI organization ("Personal") has no verification: both Individual and Business rows still show a Start button, and the Individual flow resolves to an identity check with Persona ("Start ID Check").
For an MCP-backed listing the dashboard requires all four listing URLs: websiteURL, supportURL, privacyPolicyURL and termsOfServiceURL.
Initial MCP review requires exactly five positive and three negative test cases and a reviewer-accessible demo recording URL, plus reviewer credentials if sign-in is required.
PayStage already publishes a privacy policy at https://paystage.xyz/privacy that lists recorded fields, what is not recorded, recipients and removal, which covers the privacyPolicyURL requirement.
The 2026-11-21 row recorded the path as "account + review, no money stated" and no gate, which remains true on cost but omitted the enforced identity verification now shown in the dashboard.

The public submission surface is the Plugins dashboard at platform.openai.com/plugins, whose steps are "Upload your plugin ZIP", "Complete automated checks", "Submit for review" and "Publish your plugin".

Identity verification is mandatory before submission: "All plugin submissions must come from verified individuals or organizations" and "Publishing under an unverified individual or business name will result in rejection."

The signed-in organization holds no verification: the Individual row still says "You are verifying as a solo developer." beside a Start button, and the flow opens "Start ID Check" with an identity check using our partner Persona.
For an MCP-backed listing "all four listing URLs are required": websiteURL, supportURL, privacyPolicyURL and termsOfServiceURL.
Review needs "exactly five positive and three negative cases", a reviewer-accessible demo recording URL, and reviewer credentials if sign-in is required.
PayStage already meets the privacy-policy field: https://paystage.xyz/privacy states there are "no tracking cookies and no pixels" and enumerates recorded fields, recipients and removal.
Row 350 recorded "account + review, no money stated" and "gate: none", having read the catalogue rather than the submission portal.
